expect: Most people walk soon after surgery and keep getting stronger over the next few weeks. Your surgeon will give you your own timeline.

items.text: Work with a therapist on hip and core strength
items.detail: Therapists often focus on hip bending, balance, and core stability to help you move safely after surgery.

items.text: Practice using crutches or a walker
items.detail: Getting used to moving with support before surgery can make the first days at home much easier.

items.text: Ask if you will need crutches
items.detail: Most people use crutches for a period after surgery, but how long varies. Hospitals often supply them, so ask before surgery day.
Some surgeons use a brace to limit hip rotation; others do not, so follow your surgeon's plan.

items.text: Plan for ice after exercise and surgery
items.detail: Ice packs for 15-20 minutes a few times a day can ease swelling and pain; follow your team's advice on how often and for how long.

items.text: Set up a recovery area on the main floor
items.detail: Stairs can be tricky on crutches, so living on one level for the first days can help if your home allows it.

items.text: Ask if a raised toilet seat or shower chair would help
items.detail: Not everyone needs these after hip arthroscopy. Your surgeon or therapist can say whether they suit your procedure.

items.text: Clear a wide path for walking
items.detail: You will move slowly with crutches, so remove rugs and clutter from your main walking route.

items.text: Bring a list of current medicines
items.detail: Your surgeon needs to know all medicines and supplements you take, including over-the-counter drugs.

items.text: Focus on walking and hip strength
items.detail: Therapy often builds up walking distance and hip control over the first few weeks.
Driving is often possible around 6 weeks, once you walk without crutches and can brake safely in an emergency; your surgeon will advise.
Many people may put full weight on the leg as comfort allows, but some are limited for a few weeks; follow your surgeon's plan.

items.text: Ask which hip movements to avoid
items.detail: Many surgeons advise avoiding sudden or twisting movements for a while, but the rules depend on what was done. Follow your surgeon's plan.

items.text: Ask about lifting and work restrictions
items.detail: Desk jobs may be possible within a couple of weeks, active jobs by about 6 weeks, and very heavy jobs closer to 3 months; your surgeon will advise.

items.text: Confirm which version of surgery you had
items.detail: Repair versus decompression changes recovery time, so ask your surgeon exactly what was done.

items.text: Ask when physical therapy will start
items.detail: Early sessions usually begin within the first days to 2 weeks, with gentle exercises done several times a day as taught.
